title: Context Reuse and Retry Budgets
summary: Work through Context Reuse and Retry Budgets.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Context Reuse and Retry Budgets**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Economics, § Context Reuse and Retry Budgets
blocks.md: Across the turns of a repair, the same prompt prefix recurs call after call. Context engineering arranges the request so that the stable part comes first, and the serving system keeps the key-value (KV) attention state of that prefix so the next call need not recompute it. Reuse lowers cost, but it is not free, and it competes with two other purchases the runtime can make: compacting the context, which shortens the prompt but discards reusable state, and buying more attempts, which raises coverage but multiplies the bill.

questions.q: The section **Context Reuse and Retry Budgets** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Deterministic code, a fixed workflow, a bounded loop, and delegation are compared under one acceptance contract by cost per resolved task including human fallback, not by automated cost per automated acceptance.

Ideal prefix reuse bills the quadratic re-send at the cached rate, which lowers its coefficient without removing it, so a compaction pays back only after enough turns to recover its rewrite and lost cache.
A speedup g applied to a fraction f of the measured critical path gives T' = T[(1-f) + f/g] and a ceiling of 1/(1-f), which a baseline profile reveals before anything is bought.
Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.
